components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1

                two digits of the fiscal year's starting calendar year. The
                fiscal year starts on 1 July, so a business-day-adjusted
                registrationDate on or after 1 July belongs to that calendar
                year's fiscal year and one before 1 July belongs to the previous
                calendar year's fiscal year. Absent when no registrationDate is
                available.

              readOnly: true

## Summary

I implemented the `riskFlag` field so the application satisfies the spec: *return `riskFlag` true when the owner is a possible duplicate, the email domain is disposable-adjacent, or the city is over its soft capacity; otherwise false.*

**Changes:**

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — Added a read-only `riskFlag` boolean property to the Owner DTO schema (which regenerates `OwnerDto` with the new field), documenting the three trigger conditions.

2. **`src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — Added:
   - A `@Mapping(target = "riskFlag", expression = "java(riskFlag(owner))")` on `toOwnerDto`.
   - `riskFlag(Owner)` — OR of the three conditions:
     - **possible duplicate** → `owner.getPossibleDuplicate()` (the persisted soft-match flag from the existing duplicate-detection rule).
     - **city over soft capacity** → `owner.getCapacityWarning()` (the existing per-city warning flag, set when the city already held ≥40 owners — the soft cap below the hard limit of 50).
     - **disposable-adjacent email** → `emailDomainDisposableAdjacent(Owner)`.
   - `emailDomainDisposableAdjacent(Owner)` + a `DISPOSABLE_ADJACENT_TOKENS` set — flags email domains that resemble throwaway/disposable providers (e.g. `mailinator.net`, `throwaway-inbox.io`) without being on the hard blocklist, which is already rejected outright at create time.

The derivation reads only persisted owner state (`possibleDuplicate`, `capacityWarning`, `email`), so `riskFlag` is stable across the create response and subsequent `GET` reads. The new `Cp58` acceptance test (normal owner → `riskFlag` false) passes, along with all 69 pre-existing tests.

Note on the design choice: the spec's "disposable-adjacent" was a new, undefined term (distinct from the existing hard disposable blocklist), and the only new test exercises the false case. I chose a reasonable, self-contained definition — domains containing known disposable-provider tokens (catching different-TLD variants and disposable signal words) — matching the phrase's intent.
